test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The corresponding sides of two similar triangles are in the ratio of 2: 3. If the area of the smaller triangle is 36 sq cm, then the area of the bigger triangle is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is the square of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Ratio of sides = 2 : 3

Ratio of areas = 2² : 3² = 4 : 9

Given: Area of **smaller triangle** (4 units) = 36 sq cm

⇒ 1 unit = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 sq cm

⇒ Area of **bigger triangle** (9 units) = 9 × 9 = 81 sq cm

**∴ The correct answer is 81 sq cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of sides (s₁ : s₂) = 2 : 3

Area of smaller triangle (A₁) = 36 sq cm

**Formula Used:**

Area₁ / Area₂ = (side₁ / side₂)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22a8569cd84ceec0907f1d171c212bd2a8dfc9209ee9fe3ea023a532eb0c36f6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area(Smaller) / Area(Bigger) = (2 / 3)²

⇒ 36 / Area(Bigger) = 4 / 9

⇒ Area(Bigger) × 4 = 36 × 9

⇒ Area(Bigger) = (36 × 9) ÷ 4

⇒ Area(Bigger) = 9 × 9

⇒ Area(Bigger) = 81 sq cm

**∴ The correct answer is 81 sq cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area Ratio Theorem

For any two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, or perimeters.

Perimeter Ratio

The ratio of the **perimeters** of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P₁/P₂ = s₁/s₂.

Conditions for Similarity

Triangles are similar if they satisfy **AA** (Angle-Angle), **SAS** (Side-Angle-Side), or **SSS** (Side-Side-Side) criteria.</p
